headline: Oppenheimer says businesses now expect their AI software spending to prove its worth in measurable results.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a research firm's view on how companies are judging AI spending.
importance_line: Software buyers and investors are told AI spending is being judged on measurable returns, which is one firm's view and names stocks Oppenheimer favors or doubts.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports that investment bank Oppenheimer says companies' AI spending is moving from experiments toward measurable financial returns, with finance chiefs weighing AI costs alongside labour. Oppenheimer says Microsoft, Oracle, Salesforce and ServiceNow each have an AI business worth more than USD 1 billion.
notes: Yahoo Finance page has no named author or Oppenheimer link; credited as Yahoo Finance citing Oppenheimer. Google News also lists an Oppenheimer "top software application stocks" item dated 28 Sep 2026 (Investing.com), which may be related earlier coverage; not confirmed to be the same note. Article names stocks Oppenheimer prefers or is wary of (Microsoft, ServiceNow, Braze; Figma and SoundHound cautious): these are the firm's views, not ours, and no buy or sell advice is given here.
